name: FAST - Premium Fashion Storefront Design Challenge (48 hrs)
description:
**CHALLENGE SUMMARY**
Welcome to the **Premium Fashion Storefront Design Challenge.**

Our client is rebuilding its online store from scratch. In this challenge, we need your creative solution to design the new store, from the home page to the order confirmation. The new design should improve the customer experience and be consistent with the client's brand guidelines.
Please read the challenge specifications carefully and let us know if you have any questions in the forums.

**CHALLENGE OBJECTIVES:**
* Design a new online store for the client, from the home page to the order confirmation.
* Improve the customer experience of browsing, choosing and buying products.
* Make the store consistent with the client's brand guidelines.

**ROLLING CHECKPOINT:**
*Notice this is a FAST single-round challenge but you do need to do some quick research and think about our user!*
- We will have 5 Rolling Checkpoint Prizes at $50 each.

We will provide rolling checkpoint feedback to the submissions that are received by Saturday, October 24, 2026 11:45 AM EDT. You can submit any screen(s) that you would like to receive feedback for. You can submit PNG/JPG of your files without the source files included.
- **Challenge Start:** Friday, October 23, 2026
- **Rolling Checkpoint Start:** Saturday, October 24, 2026, 11:45 AM EDT.
- **Final Designs:** Sunday, October 25, 2026, 11:45 AM EDT.

**Notes about Rolling Checkpoint:**
- PM and Copilot will be available to review early submissions and provide Rolling Checkpoint Feedback.
- We will answer questions and provide Rolling Feedback as fast as possible.
- You must watch the Forum for your feedback.

---
**ROLLING CHECKPOINT REQUIREMENTS**
Submit the following screens for checkpoint feedback:
01) Home
03) Product Page

**FINAL SUBMISSION REQUIREMENTS**
Submit all screens with the checkpoint feedback applied:
01) Home
02) Product Listing
03) Product Page
04) Cart
05) Checkout
06) Order Confirmation
07) Additional States

name: Airport Retail Media Platform
description:
## Challenge overview

Build a locally runnable, demo-ready prototype of an airport retail media platform: ads and promotions on airport screens, triggered by live flight and passenger-flow data. The POC must win the room in a 15-minute demo to airport operator and advertiser stakeholders using a deployed URL demo playground.

## Product context and roles

The platform provides airport digital-screen inventory to retailers, F&B outlets and airlines, and times each ad to the passengers actually in front of the screen. Flight data from the AODB tells the system who is where and for how long: a delayed Dubai flight at Gate 42 means 280 international passengers with 40 extra minutes near duty-free.

| Role | Who | What they want from the platform |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Platform Admin | Platform operator | Network health, revenue, screen uptime, bugs and incidents, onboarding of vendors, locations, F&B retailers, airlines and screens |
| Retailer | Shop or F&B outlet on the airside | Run and reuse campaigns, live impressions and conversions, passenger flow near the store, time-limited promo codes, campaign history and ROI |
| Media Manager | Platform operator's ad sales and inventory team | Sell and schedule inventory, approve creatives, pricing and yield, occupancy of every screen and slot, advertiser reporting |
| Airline Representative | Airline marketing or station manager | Gate and boarding-area messaging for their own flights, upgrade and lounge upsell, delay goodwill offers, co-branded promotions with retailers |
| Passenger (simulated) | Traveller in front of a screen | Relevant offers, flight info next to the ad, scan-to-claim QR with a countdown, shareable codes for family |

No login exists. A role switcher in the header changes the persona, and the retailer and airline views also switch between sample companies (for example, a duty-free store, a coffee chain, a low-cost airline and a full-service airline, all with fictional names).

## Data model and adapters

All airport data is mocked, but every mock must look exactly like what a real source would send, so going live means writing one new adapter and nothing else. The app core only ever sees a canonical internal model; adapters translate source formats into it.

| Source standard | What it supplies | POC mock format | Canonical entities |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| AODB flight movements (any AODB vendor) | Schedule, estimated and actual times (A-CDM: TOBT, TSAT, AIBT, AOBT), stand, gate, check-in counters, belt, aircraft, pax count, status, delay codes | CSV or JSON, one row per flight leg, 33 columns as in the sample AODB file | `Flight`, `GateAssignment`, `AircraftType` |
| IATA AIDX XML | Real-time flight-leg updates (`IATA_AIDX_FlightLegNotifRQ`): status changes, gate changes, delays | XML messages pushed on a simulated feed | `FlightEvent` |
| ACI ACRIS (FIWARE Smart Data Models) | Terminals, concourses, checkpoints, zones, passenger queues and queue measurements | NGSI-LD style JSON entities | `Terminal`, `Zone`, `Checkpoint`, `QueueMeasurement` |
| Platform-owned (no standard) | Screens, retailers, outlets, campaigns, creatives, promo codes, impressions, redemptions | Tables in the app database | `Screen`, `Advertiser`, `Outlet`, `Campaign`, `Creative`, `PromoCode`, `Impression`, `Redemption` |

**Adapter contract.** Each source has an interface such as `FlightSource.stream(): AsyncIterable<FlightEvent>` with a mock implementation and a stub `Live` implementation. Switching is a single config value (`FLIGHT_SOURCE=mock-aidx | vendor-api`).

**Derived signal: passenger presence.** The core value is the `ZonePresence` estimate per zone and per 5-minute window: how many passengers, which nationalities and destinations, domestic or international, and their dwell time. It is computed from flights at nearby gates (pax count × time to boarding) and ACRIS queue data. Every ad decision and every dashboard KPI uses it.

**Reference samples** are attached to the challenge, re-labelled to the fictional airport before sharing (`aodb-samples/`): a synthetic one-day AODB file (320 flights), an illustrative AIDX flight-leg message, and the public ACRIS entity schemas.

## Audience matching and decision rules

Every ad slot on every screen goes to the campaign whose target audience best matches the estimated crowd in front of that screen for the next few minutes. The crowd profile, the rules, the scores and the reason for each decision must be visible and understandable in every role.

**AI decision pipeline:** evidence-first crowd-to-screen matching. Every ad decision comes from measured data only: AODB and AIDX flight events, ACRIS queue and zone gauges, and live screen, scan and redemption metrics. Each input carries its source, timestamp and freshness. The AI scores and ranks campaigns against the crowd profile, but a decision is only executed once deterministic checks confirm it: every input it cites must exist in a trusted feed and be fresh enough, every hard rule must pass, and the score must be reproducible from the logged inputs. If any check fails, the AI’s choice is rejected and the screen falls back to a rule-based default. Nothing the AI asserts is used unless it traces back to a recorded data point, so a hallucinated fact cannot reach a screen. Every decision is logged with its evidence trail, so any role can audit why an ad played.

### Crowd profile: what the system knows about the crowd

A profile is built per flight, then rolled up per screen and per 5-minute window, weighted by how close each gate is to the screen and how long until boarding. All attributes are aggregated shares ("62% holiday travellers"), never data about a person.

| Attribute | Values | POC mock source | Real source later |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Destination and arrival source | City, country, region; domestic or international; connecting from | AODB origin, destination, via | AODB |
| Trip purpose | Business, holiday, visiting family and friends, student, religious | Route type, day of week and time of day rules, mocked shares | Airline aggregated booking mix, surveys |
| Party type | Solo, couple, family with children, group | Mocked per route and season (school holidays raise families) | Airline aggregated PNR statistics |
| Age band | Under 12, 12–17, 18–24, 25–34, 35–44, 45–54, 55+ | Mocked distribution per route | Airline aggregates, anonymous audience sensors |
| Gender split | % female, % male | Mocked per route | Airline aggregates, anonymous audience sensors |
| Cabin and spend tier | Economy, premium economy, business; frequent-flyer share | Aircraft seat configuration + mocked fare mix | Airline aggregates |
| Nationality and language | Top 3 nationalities and languages | Route | APIS aggregates (international) |
| Time context | Dwell minutes to boarding, delay minutes, time of day, festival or holiday period | AODB times + event calendar | AODB |
| Crowd size | Passengers in the zone now and in the next 30 min | Pax count × gate proximity | AODB + ACRIS queue and sensor data |

The mock generator must give every flight a profile like this, and the profiles must be plausible: a Monday 07:00 domestic flight skews to business travellers aged 25–44; a Friday evening holiday route skews to families and couples.

### Campaign targeting: what the advertiser asks for

- **Segment weights:** how much each segment matters, 0 to 1 (for example, Family 1.0, Holiday 0.8, Business 0.1).
- **Hard filters:** conditions that must be true (international only, destination in the Gulf region, dwell of 15 minutes or more, at least 100 passengers in the zone).
- **Placement:** zones, screens or gates, plus a schedule.
- **Budget and limits:** total budget, daily cap, frequency cap per screen.
- **Triggers (optional):** delay over N minutes, gate change, boarding starts, festival day.

### Decision pipeline: run per screen for every slot (about every 15 seconds)

1. **Profile:** build the crowd profile for this screen's catchment for the next slot window.
2. **Filter:** drop campaigns that fail a hard rule: schedule, placement, approval status, brand safety, domestic or international, destination, minimum crowd size, budget exhausted.
3. **Score:** score every remaining campaign based on smart, optimized algorithm and/or AI Agent decision based on LLMs.
4. **Apply business rules:** airline priority in its own boarding window, competitor separation (no two perfume brands back to back), frequency cap, budget pacing.
5. **Choose and log:** play the highest score and store the full decision: profile, candidates, scores, and the winning reason.
6. **Learn:** scans and redemptions per segment update each campaign's conversion estimate, so the next decisions improve.

**Worked example (must be reproducible in the demo).** Gate 42 at 14:10. The crowd is flight XY501 to DXB (240 pax, delayed 45 min) plus flight ZQ88 to a beach destination (180 pax). Profile: holiday 58%, family 31%, business 22%, international 57%, median dwell 52 min.

| Candidate campaign | Targets | Audience match | Boost | Final score | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Duty-free perfume, 15% off | International, holiday, adults 25–54 | 71% | 1.5 (delay rule) | 0.86 | Plays |
| Toy store, buy 2 get 1 | Family with children | 49% | 1.0 | 0.52 | Next in rotation |
| Business lounge day pass | Business, premium cabin | 18% | 1.0 | 0.21 | Filtered to other gates |

### How each role sees the matching

| Role | What they see and control |
| --- | --- |
| Platform Admin | Rule engine settings (global weights, exploration %, frequency caps, competitor separation), a searchable decision log, and the version of the segment model in use |
| Retailer | Live audience-match preview while building a campaign ("matches 64% of the crowd at Gates 40–45 from 14:00 to 16:00; expected 3,100 impressions and 95 redemptions"), performance by segment after the run ("families redeemed 3x more"), and suggested weight changes |
| Media Manager | Segment heatmap of segment × hour × zone to price inventory, a conflict view explaining why campaign A beat campaign B, and manual pin or override with a reason |
| Airline Representative | Aggregated crowd profile of their own flights, partner offers ranked by fit for their passengers, and what played at their gates and why |
| Passenger screen | A "Why this ad?" overlay showing the crowd profile bars, the top 3 candidates with scores, and the winning rule |

## Screens per role

Each role gets one main dashboard and up to three sub-pages, all sharing one design system and one live clock (the simulation time). Items marked **Must** are scored; **Should** items earn extra points.

### 1. Platform Admin (operator console)

- **Must:** Live network map of the terminal (T1/T2 floor plan, stylised SVG is fine) with every screen as a dot, coloured online / degraded / offline, and a heat overlay of passenger presence.
- **Must:** KPI strip: screens online %, ad plays today, impressions, revenue today (configurable currency), active campaigns, average screen latency.
- **Must:** Incident and bug tracker: auto-raised alerts (screen offline > 5 min, feed lag, failed creative), with severity, owner and status.
- **Must:** Master data management (list + create/edit forms): vendors, outlets and F&B retailers, airlines, locations (terminal, zone, gate), screens (size, orientation, zone, nearest gates).
- **Should:** Data feed health: AODB / AIDX / ACRIS feed status, messages per minute, last message time, adapter in use.
- **Should:** Performance panel: API p95 latency, playlist build time, uptime over 7 days.

### 2. Retailer (shop or F&B outlet)

- **Must:** Live dashboard for the selected outlet: impressions, scans, redemptions, conversion rate, revenue attributed, all ticking in real time.
- **Must:** Passenger flow near my store: footfall in the zone for the next 2 hours, derived from upcoming departures, with top destinations and nationalities ("Next 60 min: 1,240 pax, 38% international, top: DXB, LHR, SIN").
- **Must:** Campaign builder: pick creative, target zones/screens, audience rules (destination, domestic/international, dwell time, delay), schedule, budget; then preview on a mock screen.
- **Must:** Creative library: upload or reuse ad pages and templates, duplicate a past campaign in one click.
- **Must:** Promo codes: time-boxed codes and QR on screen that expire when the crowd moves on (for example, valid until the linked flight's boarding closes), with a share-to-family option producing a second code.
- **Must:** Campaign history: past campaigns with spend, impressions, redemptions, ROI, and a "run again" action.
- **Should (proposed):** Trigger rules: "if flight to DXB is delayed > 30 min, show 15% off at Gate 40–45 screens".
- **Should (proposed):** Stock-aware offers: pause a promo when the item is out of stock (mock toggle).
- **Should (proposed):** Budget pacing and simple A/B creative comparison.

### 3. Media Manager (operator ad sales and inventory)

- **Must:** Inventory calendar: every screen × hour, showing booked, available, and premium slots (premium = high predicted footfall).
- **Must:** Yield and pricing: suggested price per slot driven by predicted passenger presence; occupancy % and revenue forecast for the next 7 days.
- **Must:** Approval queue: creatives and campaigns awaiting review, with approve/reject and brand-safety checklist.
- **Must:** Advertiser overview: top advertisers by spend, campaigns running, under-delivering campaigns flagged.
- **Should (proposed):** Package builder: bundle screens (for example, "International departures premium pack") to sell to brands.
- **Should (proposed):** One-click advertiser report (PDF or shareable link).

### 4. Airline Representative

- **Must:** My flights today: list and timeline of the airline's departures at the airport with gate, status, delay, load factor.
- **Must:** Gate-area messaging: schedule sponsored content on screens at my gates for my boarding window, for example upgrade offers, lounge passes, destination partners.
- **Must:** Delay goodwill automation: when a flight is delayed past a threshold, auto-push a meal or lounge voucher co-funded with an F&B retailer to gate screens.
- **Should (proposed):** Co-marketing marketplace: retailers offer deals to an airline's passengers ("Airline X passengers get 10% at Café Y"), the airline accepts with one click.
- **Should (proposed):** Performance: impressions and redemptions among the airline's own passengers.

### 5. Passenger screen simulator

- **Must:** Full-screen view of a chosen physical screen (pick by gate or zone), rendering the current playlist in a 9:16 or 16:9 frame.
- **Must:** Context strip with nearby flights (FIDS-style) next to the ad.
- **Must:** Dynamic ad selection that visibly changes as simulation time moves and flights board, delay or depart.
- **Must:** Promo QR with a live countdown; scanning it with a real phone opens a mobile claim page served on the laptop's LAN address (the QR encodes the LAN IP, configurable) that records a redemption, visible immediately in the Retailer dashboard.
- **Must:** "Why this ad?" overlay showing the crowd profile, the top 3 candidate scores and the winning rule (see Audience matching).

## WOW features and demo script

The WOW is cause and effect across roles in under a minute: a flight event in the AODB feed changes what a passenger sees, the passenger claims a code, and money shows up on the retailer's dashboard.

**Required WOW features**

- Simulation control bar (visible to all roles): play, pause, speed 1x / 10x / 60x, jump to time, and "inject event" buttons (delay flight, gate change, screen goes offline).
- Live cause-and-effect: an injected AIDX delay updates the Airline view, re-plans gate screens, triggers the retailer's delay rule and raises the passenger count in the zone, all within 2 seconds.
- Split-screen demo mode: passenger screen on the left, any role dashboard on the right.
- GenAI creative assistant *(mocked offline, pluggable real provider)*: type a brief ("Festive sweets, 20% off, families flying domestic") and get a ready ad page in the template, in English and a second configured language.
- Smart recommendation: "Best 3 slots for this campaign tomorrow" with predicted impressions.

## Technical requirements

The app must run on a clean laptop with one command, offline, and look like a finished product.

| Area | Requirement |
| --- | --- |
| Stack | Open: any modern web frontend and backend framework. It must be a widely used, actively maintained open-source stack, and the submitter justifies the choice in the README |
| Architecture | Separate frontend and backend; REST or GraphQL API plus WebSocket or SSE for live updates; adapter layer isolated from business logic |
| Storage | Embedded or containerised database with migrations and a seed script; no paid or cloud services required |
| Start | One command (`docker compose up` or equivalent) brings up everything on `localhost` |
| Playground | Fully working URL of playground deployed your solution for review(only during challenge duration) |
| Mock data | Generator that produces 1 day at the fictional airport, with fictional airline, brand and outlet names: ~900 flights, ~180 screens, 40 outlets, 10 airlines, 25 campaigns with 30 days of history |
| Feeds | Mock AODB snapshot (CSV/JSON), AIDX XML message stream, ACRIS JSON entities, each behind an adapter interface |
| AI | Pluggable provider; default mock returns template-based creatives so the demo works with no API key |
| UI quality | Responsive at 1440px and 1920px; dark "control room" theme for Admin, light theme for business roles; mobile layout for the promo claim page; white-label product with a theme config (name, logo, colours) and no real airport, airline or brand marks; UI and ad content in English plus one configurable second language (i18n) |
| Performance | Dashboard updates within 2 s of a feed event; 60x simulation runs without UI lag |
| Docs | README, architecture diagram, adapter guide, API spec (OpenAPI or schema) |

**Out of scope:** real authentication, payments, real screen hardware (CMS/player), production hosting, and any per-passenger data. Targeting is aggregated by flight, zone and time window only; no boarding-pass, identity or device tracking.

## Deliverables

1. Source code (frontend + backend)
2. One-command local start (`docker compose up` or one equivalent command), seeded mock data included.
3. A README with setup, architecture, and a data adapter guide.
4. **A fully working playground URL where the reviewer[s] will be able to review your submission deployed and pre-configured. It should be available during the challenge duration.**

name: Enterprise AI Customer Experience Resolution System: Gemini CX & Telco
description:
Topcoder is seeking production-grade solutions for an **Enterprise AI Customer Experience Resolution System** built on Google Cloud Platform (GCP) and **Gemini Customer Experience (Gemini CX)** architecture.

In this challenge, you will act as a Lead Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE). You will design, build, and deploy an end-to-end, multi-agent AI customer support resolution engine for a major Telecommunications / Communications Service Provider (CSP). The system must securely integrate with legacy backend services (Billing, Network Diagnostics, Account Auth), feature robust multi-agent orchestration, implement enterprise-grade security protocols, and provide complete observability and telemetry.

**Objective:** Build a proof-of-concept (PoC) enterprise agentic solution capable of autonomously handling complex customer scenarios—such as authenticating a subscriber, running broadband hardware diagnostics, resolving billing disputes, or performing automated escalation—using Gemini CX / Google Cloud AI frameworks.

## Challenge Goal

Complete and productionize the supplied AI customer-experience solution so that it can:

* Understand customer requests using Gemini
* Ask relevant clarification questions
* Manage conversation and workflow context
* Coordinate agents, workflows, and enterprise tools
* Authenticate customers before accessing protected information
* Enforce authorization outside the AI model
* Integrate with modern and legacy enterprise systems
* Produce responses grounded in verified enterprise data
* Perform supported actions only after validation and confirmation
* Handle AI and enterprise-service failures safely
* Escalate unresolved requests with useful context
* Generate structured logs, traces, events, and operational metrics
* Support repeatable automated evaluation
* Provide a credible Google Cloud deployment approach
* Enable another engineering team to understand and extend the solution

The productionized solution is the practical evidence used to validate and rank competitors. Building the solution is not the final business outcome of the challenge.

## Challenge Type

**AI Exponential League Practical Qualification and Productionization Challenge**

This challenge combines:

* Existing codebase analysis
* Gemini integration
* Conversational AI
* Agentic architecture
* Workflow and tool orchestration
* Secure API implementation
* Authentication and authorization
* Enterprise integration
* Legacy-system adaptation
* Data pipelines
* Telemetry and observability
* Reliability engineering
* Automated testing
* Google Cloud deployment planning
* Technical handover

**Participants may use:**

* A single controlled AI agent
* Multiple specialized agents
* Deterministic workflow orchestration
* A hybrid AI and rules-based architecture
* Google-supported agent frameworks
* A custom implementation

Framework choice alone will not determine the score.

Participants must improve the supplied starter solution rather than replace it with an unrelated implementation.

## Business Scenario

A telecommunications provider uses separate enterprise systems for:

* Customer identity
* Customer profiles
* Accounts and subscriptions
* Billing information
* Product and service eligibility
* Network and service status
* Technical diagnostics
* Support-case management

The provider has started developing an AI-powered customer-experience solution, but the current implementation is not ready for production.

The supplied solution contains gaps such as:

* Incomplete Gemini integration
* Weak or incomplete agent orchestration
* Stubbed enterprise integrations
* Missing authorization controls
* Incomplete legacy-system handling
* Unsafe enterprise-action execution
* Limited failure handling
* Missing telemetry and traces
* Incomplete automated tests
* Limited deployment documentation

Participants must transform the starter solution into a secure, reliable, observable, and deployment-ready proof of capability.

The system is a technical assessment environment. It must use only supplied or synthetic customer data and must not connect to real customer records.

## Supplied Starter Package

The challenge repository will include:

* Partially implemented source code
* Basic customer interaction interface or conversation runner
* Initial Gemini integration or provider adapter
* Stubbed agent or workflow orchestration
* Mock authentication service
* Customer-profile service
* Account and subscription service
* Billing or service-information service
* Network-status or diagnostics service
* Case-management service
* Legacy telecom service
* Sample customer and account data
* Test users and roles
* Mandatory customer scenarios
* Failure-simulation controls
* API documentation and schemas
* Initial architecture documentation
* Known technical gaps
* Sample environment configuration

The same starter package, scenarios, test data, and failure controls will be provided to all competitors.

Participants may refactor individual components where necessary, but the required workflows and supplied enterprise integrations must remain reviewable.

## Target Users

**1. Customer**

The customer uses the solution to:

* Ask account or service questions
* Report service issues
* Request technical assistance
* Review available service options
* Perform supported account or service actions
* Receive a verified resolution or escalation reference

**2. Customer Support Representative**

The support representative receives escalated requests containing:

* Request summary
* Verified customer context
* Completed workflow steps
* Enterprise systems already accessed
* Retrieved evidence
* Failed tools or integrations
* Pending actions
* Recommended next step
* Request or trace identifier

**3. Operations and Engineering User**

The operations or engineering user reviews:

* Workflow executions
* Agent and tool activity
* Integration performance
* Authentication and authorization events
* Failed requests
* Escalations
* Operational metrics
* Application health

## Core User Journey

1. A customer submits a natural-language request.
2. Gemini interprets the request and extracts relevant information.
3. The system asks for clarification if required information is missing.
4. The customer authenticates when protected information or actions are involved.
5. Deterministic authorization logic validates access.
6. The orchestrator selects the appropriate agent, workflow, or enterprise tool.
7. Enterprise data is retrieved and normalized.
8. The system validates the returned information.
9. A grounded response or proposed action is presented.
10. The customer confirms any consequential action.
11. The enterprise action is executed and verified.
12. The system returns a confirmed outcome or creates an escalation.
13. The complete execution is recorded through structured events and traces.
14. Operational metrics are updated from actual workflow activity.

## Functional Requirements

**1. Gemini and Conversational AI**

The solution must use Gemini meaningfully within the required customer workflows.

**Gemini may be used for:**

* Intent classification
* Entity extraction
* Request interpretation
* Clarification-question generation
* Workflow planning
* Agent routing
* Tool selection
* Enterprise-information synthesis
* Grounded response generation
* Escalation summarization

**Participants must document:**

* Gemini model or service used
* Where the model is invoked
* Purpose of each model invocation
* Context supplied to the model
* Prompt or agent instructions
* Structured output definitions
* Output validation
* Safety controls
* Failure behavior
* Decisions enforced outside the model

Authentication, authorization, record ownership, confirmation, and protected business actions must be enforced through deterministic application logic.

A submission implemented entirely through fixed responses or hardcoded scenario branches will not qualify.

**2. Agent Architecture and Orchestration**

Participants must complete or improve the supplied agentic or workflow architecture.

**The solution may use:**

* A primary orchestrator with specialized agents
* A controlled tool-using agent
* Multiple cooperating agents
* A deterministic workflow with AI-assisted steps
* A hybrid architecture

**The implementation must demonstrate:**

* Clear agent or component responsibilities
* Controlled tool access
* Conversation and workflow state management
* Routing and delegation logic
* Validation before tool execution
* Loop prevention
* Completion and termination conditions
* Timeout and error handling
* Human review and escalation points

**If multiple agents are used, participants must explain:**

* Why each agent is required
* What information it can access
* Which tools it may execute
* How context is transferred
* How conflicting results are handled
* How unnecessary agent calls are avoided
* How the workflow determines completion

Using more agents will not automatically receive a higher score. The architecture must be appropriate, controlled, reliable, and maintainable.

**3. Customer Authentication and Authorization**

The solution must authenticate customers before accessing protected information or executing protected actions.

**The implementation must:**

* Use the supplied authentication service or an approved equivalent
* Maintain authentication state appropriately
* Handle invalid and expired authentication
* Prevent one customer from accessing another customer’s records
* Enforce record ownership or role permissions
* Restrict tools according to the authenticated user and workflow state
* Validate model-generated tool parameters
* Record authentication and authorization events
* Protect credentials and tokens from the AI model
* Avoid exposing sensitive authentication information in logs or traces

The AI model must never be the sole authority for granting access.

A simulated authentication flow is acceptable because the challenge uses synthetic data, but the flow and enforcement must be technically meaningful.

**4. Enterprise and Legacy-System Integration**

The solution must integrate with the supplied enterprise services and the legacy telecom service.

**The integration layer must handle:**

* Request validation
* Response validation
* Data normalization
* Enterprise authentication
* Error-code mapping
* Timeouts
* Safe and limited retries
* Missing or partial data
* Malformed responses
* Rate limits
* Duplicate requests
* Failed enterprise operations

Enterprise systems must be accessed through controlled tools, services, or adapters. Gemini must not receive unrestricted access to raw enterprise endpoints.

**Legacy Telecom Adapter**

**The supplied legacy service may include:**

* XML requests or responses
* Inconsistent field names
* Legacy status codes
* Unusual error codes
* Missing optional fields
* Slow responses
* Intermittent failures
* Older authentication behavior

**Participants must complete or implement an adapter that:**

* Communicates with the legacy interface.
* Validates the returned response.
* Converts the response into a consistent internal model.
* Maps legacy errors into application-level errors.
* Prevents raw legacy-system behavior from leaking into the AI and customer layers.
* Produces useful diagnostic events without exposing protected data.

The legacy service must not be bypassed or replaced with hardcoded results.

**5. Grounded and Trustworthy Responses**

Customer-facing responses must be grounded in customer input and verified enterprise information.

**The solution must distinguish between:**

* Customer-provided information
* Retrieved enterprise information
* AI-generated interpretation
* Assumptions
* Recommendations
* Confirmed actions
* Unverified information

**The solution must not:**

* Invent customer or account records
* Generate unsupported charges, plans, outages, cases, or reference numbers
* Present assumptions as verified facts
* Claim that a tool was called when it was not
* Report a failed action as successful
* Replace unavailable data with fabricated values
* Hide materially conflicting enterprise information

If required information is unavailable or unclear, the system must ask for clarification, provide a qualified response, use an approved fallback, or escalate the request.

**6. Clarification and Context Management**

The solution must identify incomplete or ambiguous customer requests.

**It must:**

* Determine what information is missing
* Ask a relevant and specific clarification question
* Preserve previously supplied information
* Resume the existing workflow after clarification
* Avoid asking for information already provided
* Avoid unsupported assumptions
* Avoid calling protected or consequential tools prematurely

Generic requests for “more information” will receive limited credit when the missing information can be identified precisely.

**7. Controlled Enterprise Action**

The solution must support at least one consequential enterprise action.

**Examples include:**

* Creating a support case
* Scheduling technical assistance
* Submitting a service-change request
* Updating an account preference
* Requesting a supported plan change

**Before completing the action, the solution must:**

* Authenticate the customer.
* Verify authorization.
* Validate the requested action and parameters.
* Present an understandable action summary.
* Obtain explicit customer confirmation.
* Execute the controlled enterprise tool.
* Validate the backend response.
* Report success only after confirmed execution.
* Return a valid reference identifier where applicable.
* Record the action and result.
* Prevent accidental duplicate execution.

A proposed or recommended action must not be shown as completed.

**8. Failure Handling and Human Escalation**

**The solution must safely handle:**

* Gemini provider failure
* Enterprise API failure
* Network timeout
* Rate limit
* Invalid or expired authentication
* Unauthorized requests
* Missing or conflicting enterprise data
* Malformed responses
* Failed enterprise actions
* Duplicate action requests
* Internal processing failures

**The implementation must:**

* Detect and classify the failure
* Preserve relevant workflow state
* Avoid fabricating an outcome
* Retry only when safe and appropriate
* Limit retry attempts
* Prevent duplicate consequential actions
* Provide a clear customer-facing explanation
* Use a documented fallback where available
* Escalate when safe completion is not possible
* Record the failure in logs, traces, and metrics

**An escalation record must include:**

* Customer request summary
* Available verified context
* Completed workflow steps
* Enterprise systems accessed
* Relevant evidence
* Failed tools or integrations
* Error summary
* Pending action
* Recommended next step
* Request or trace identifier

The receiving representative should be able to continue the request without requiring the customer to repeat the entire interaction.

**9. Data Pipeline, Telemetry, and Observability**

The solution must produce structured events for important workflow activity.

**Events should include, where applicable:**

* Session started
* Request received
* Intent classified
* Clarification requested
* Authentication attempted
* Authentication succeeded or failed
* Authorization allowed or denied
* Agent invoked
* Tool invoked
* Tool completed or failed
* Retry performed
* Confirmation requested
* Confirmation received
* Enterprise action completed
* Escalation created
* Workflow resolved
* Workflow failed

Each event must contain a correlation or trace identifier.

**Telemetry Pipeline**

**The telemetry pipeline must:**

* Accept structured application events
* Validate event formats
* Associate events with a request or session
* Support request-level investigation
* Support operational metrics
* Handle invalid events safely
* Avoid unnecessary sensitive-data storage
* Workflow Trace

**Reviewers must be able to inspect:**

* Trace identifier
* Workflow steps
* Agents or components invoked
* Enterprise tools called
* Sanitized input and output summaries
* Execution duration
* Success or failure status
* Retry and fallback events
* Authorization decisions
* Confirmation events
* Final outcome
* Escalation reason

Passwords, tokens, secrets, unnecessary personal data, and protected model instructions must not appear in the trace.

**Operational View**

The solution must show metrics generated from actual application events, such as:

Total sessions
Resolution rate
Escalation rate
Failure rate
Average workflow duration
Tool-call success rate
Failures by integration
Authentication failures
Authorization denials
Agent and tool usage
Retry frequency
Gemini latency and failures
Human handoff rate

Static or manually entered monitoring data will not satisfy this requirement.

## Mandatory Evaluation Scenarios

Every submission will be reviewed using the same scenarios, test users, data, and failure conditions.

**1. Grounded Customer Inquiry**

* A customer requests protected account, subscription, billing, or service information.
* The solution must authenticate the customer, retrieve the correct authorized record, normalize the enterprise response, and return a grounded answer.

**2. Ambiguous Request**

* A customer provides insufficient information.
* The solution must identify the missing information, ask a specific clarification question, preserve context, and continue after clarification.

**3. Multi-System Issue Resolution**

* A customer reports an issue requiring multiple enterprise systems.
* The solution must coordinate the necessary agents or tools, preserve context, reconcile the returned information, and resolve or safely escalate the request.

**4. Protected Enterprise Action**

* An authenticated customer requests a supported action.
* The solution must validate, authorize, summarize, confirm, execute, verify, and record the action while preventing duplicate execution.

**5. Unauthorized Access Attempt**

* An authenticated customer attempts to access another customer’s record.
* The solution must deny access through deterministic authorization logic, avoid retrieving or exposing the protected record, and record the denial.

**6. Legacy-System Request**

* A customer request requires information from the supplied legacy telecom service.
* The solution must call the service, process its legacy format, normalize the response, map errors, and use the result within the customer workflow.

**7. Enterprise-Service Failure**

* A required enterprise service fails, times out, or returns incomplete information.
* The solution must avoid false success, apply safe retry behavior, preserve workflow state, and escalate where necessary.

**8. Gemini Provider Failure**

* Gemini becomes unavailable.
* The solution must detect the failure, preserve the active request, continue deterministic security controls, enter a documented fallback or degraded mode, and record the failure.

Active credentials must not be included.

**Reviewer Mode**

**Reviewer mode must continue to exercise the real:**

Reviewer mode must not be a disconnected set of static screens or predefined final responses.

**The solution must clearly show whether it is using:**

* Live AI mode
* Reviewer mode

Reviewer mode does not replace the mandatory live AI implementation.

* A static chatbot demonstration

* Architecture documents without working implementation
* A UI that does not exercise the supplied APIs
* Static telemetry or manually entered metrics
* A mock-only implementation without live Gemini integration

* A recorded demonstration that reviewers cannot reproduce

A valid submission must demonstrate:

* Meaningful Gemini usage
* Controlled agent or workflow orchestration
* Authentication and deterministic authorization
* Modern and legacy enterprise integration
* Grounded responses
* Protected enterprise-action handling
* Failure recovery and escalation
* Structured events and request-level traces
* Event-derived operational metrics
* Repeatable tests
* Deployment preparation
* Customer-team handover

## Technology Expectations

The implementation stack may be extended or adjusted where justified.

* Secure in handling synthetic customer data

A browser interface is recommended because the engagement concerns customer-experience solutions, but visual design is not the primary focus. A functional conversation runner with appropriate engineering and operational views may also be acceptable.
